title: War
full_review:
If sheer noisiness could make a film either interesting or entertaining, then "War" (Lionsgate) might rank as a classic. Throughout this dark police thriller, there are explosions, car crashes and a blizzard of flying bullets, not to mention the groans of the maimed and dying. But, alas, sound and fury by themselves are no substitute for genuine drama

.

The plot revolves around San Francisco FBI agent Jack Crawford (Jason Statham). When the legendary assassin (Jet Li) who murdered Crawford's partner, Tom Wynne (Terry Chen), returns to the City by the Bay, he sparks a war between the Japanese Yakuza gang, which is led from a distance by Shiro (Ryo Ishibashi) -- with his ruthless daughter Kira (Devon Aoki) as his local representative -- and the Chinese Triads of the city led by Chang (John Lone). Between his desire for revenge and his duty to stop the gangs from slaughtering each other, Crawford soon has his hands full.

The film's atmosphere is unremittingly grim, from the early scene in which Wynne is killed, along with his wife and daughter, to the inevitable and climactic battle between Crawford and his mysterious foe. Statham broods endlessly and could benefit from a shave and perhaps some antidepressants.

As written by Lee Anthony Smith and Gregory J. Bradley, "War" offers some interesting plot developments. But its distinctive gritty quality soon crosses the good-taste line into outright brutality, with graphic scenes of torture and dismemberment.

If this particular "War" isn't exactly hell, it certainly involves a long trip down to a very dark place.

The film contains extensive violence with gore, torture and mutilation, rear and upper female nudity, frequent rough and crude language, and occasional profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.-- parents strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
